standard_prerequisites.name: The notion of a quasi-sober topological space: every irreducible closed subset has a generic point
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Invoked in the statement (source lines 2282-2283) as a pointer to the chapter on topology
standard_prerequisites.use: Fix what has to be produced for an irreducible closed subset.

standard_prerequisites.name: The finiteness of the number of irreducible components of a closed subset of a Noetherian space, and the openness of the map on topological spaces induced by a smooth morphism
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Both are used inside the counted proof (source lines 2290-2296) as cross-chapter pointers and from the theory of presentations
standard_prerequisites.use: Decomposes the preimage of the closed subset into finitely many components and shows that the image of one of them is dense.

core_obligations: Choose a presentation meeting the subset: the proof takes an affine scheme smoothly mapping to the stack with nonempty preimage of the given irreducible closed subset (proof lines 2287-2290)
Decompose the preimage: since the scheme is Noetherian its preimage has finitely many irreducible components (proof lines 2290-2293)

Find a dense image: because the morphism is open, the image of the preimage contains a nonempty open subset of the irreducible subset, hence is dense, and therefore the image of one of the components is dense (proof lines 2293-2297)
Conclude: the image of the generic point of that component is a generic point of the given closed subset (proof lines 2297-2299)
proof_roadmap: 对不可约闭子集 T 取仿射概型 U 与光滑 U → X 使 f^{-1}(T) ≠ ∅；U Noetherian 故 f^{-1}(T) 只有有限个不可约分支 Z_1,…,Z_n。
f 开 ⇒ f|_{f^{-1}(T)} 的像含 T 的非空开子集，T 不可约故该像稠密，进而某个 f(Z_i) 稠密；取 Z_i 的 generic point ξ_i，则 f(ξ_i) 是 T 的 generic point。
difficulty_reason: The counted statement shows that the topological space of a locally Noetherian algebraic stack is quasi-sober, i.e., every irreducible closed subset has a generic point (author lemma at source lines 2279-2284, label lemma-locally-Noetherian-quasi-sober). The proof (source lines 2286-2300) picks an affine presentation meeting the closed subset, uses the Noetherianness of the presentation to decompose its preimage into finitely many irreducible components, and uses the openness of the map on spaces and the irreducibility of the subset to find a component whose image is dense, whose generic point then maps to a generic point of the subset (proof lines 2287-2299). The component argument is the content. H2.
